final_response.rationale: Python fits this task directly: its standard library covers HMAC over exact body bytes, JSON parsing, durable SQLite state, HTTP delivery, and a multi-command CLI. That keeps the implementation and offline package simpler. Veritas has useful JSON, file, HTTP, and packaging support, but it has no native SQLite or byte-oriented HTTP request body; using its Python bridge for those gaps adds managed-environment and packaging work. No comparative implementation results or benchmarks are available, so this is based on task fit, not measured performance.
conditions: I would reconsider Veritas if it gained native SQLite, byte-oriented HTTP requests, and suitable HMAC support, or if a comparable implementation showed its delivery and maintenance costs were lower.
I would reconsider either choice if the acceptance contract changed to remove durable state or exact-byte handling, since those requirements drive much of Python's advantage here.
